q: What does `cargo build -p goose-cli --bin goose` do?
options: Builds only the goose-cli package and only its `goose` binary target
Builds every workspace member and all its binaries
Builds goose-cli in release mode
Installs a prebuilt goose binary from a remote registry
explanation: -p selects one package; --bin select one binary target. Nothing implies --release.
Without -p cargo builds the default members; with -p it narrows to one package.
pip-install style behavior does not exist in cargo outside `cargo install`.

options: Edition 2021 feature unification: dev-dependency features do not leak into the normal build
Cargo may resolve two versions of any crate in the graph
The workspace compiles twice in parallel to catch race conditions
Dependencies are fetched from crates.io over HTTP/2
explanation: The resolver never splits a single semver range into two versions of the same crate in one build.
That is not a Rust concept at all.
HTTP transport defaults have nothing to do with the feature resolver.

q: Which tool installs and switches Rust toolchain versions?
options: cargo
rustup
rustc
clippy
explanation: cargo builds and manages packages; it calls whichever toolchain rustup selected.
rustc is the compiler binary itself; it does not manage toolchains.
clippy is a linter built on rustc; it runs on the active toolchain.

options: A JSON document describing workspace members but not their resolved dependency graph
The file hashes of every crate on crates.io
A human-readable log of the last build
Only the versions of rustc and cargo
explanation: It never contacts crates.io for hashes; it reflects the local workspace + lockfile.
Build logs come from cargo itself while building, not from metadata queries.
rustc/cargo versions are reported by `rustc --version`, not cargo metadata.

q: The Justfile recipe `check-everything` runs, among others:
options: `cargo fmt --all` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
`cargo build --release` and `cargo publish`
`cargo clean` and `cargo doc`
`cargo test --all` and `cargo fuzz`
explanation: It checks style, not releases: nothing builds or publishes a release.
It does not clean artifacts or generate docs.
Fuzzing is not part of the style gate for PRs.

q: What does the flag `-D warnings` in `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` do?
options: Treats every clippy warning as a hard error
Disables warnings entirely
Sets the lint level to "deny" only for the `warnings` lint group listed after it
Dumps warnings to a file called warnings
explanation: Lints are promoted, not silenced — the opposite of disabling.
It promotes ALL warnings to errors; it is not scoped to a group of the same name.
`-D` is a rustc flag for allow/warn/deny, not an output redirect.

q: Fix this compile error: `error[E0599]: no function or associated item named 'run' found for struct 'Agent'`. The most likely first thing to check is:
options: Whether the feature flag enabling that crate's `run` module is off in this build
Whether rustup is installed
Whether the Cargo.lock file is missing
Whether the file has CRLF line endings
explanation: rustup problems produce toolchain errors, not missing-item errors against your code.
A missing lockfile makes cargo regenerate it, not lose inherent items.
Line endings do not affect name resolution.
